text: Without the electromagnetic force, atomic nuclei cannot bind electrons and molecules dissolve instantaneously.
as_written: Electromagnetism holds electrons to atomic nuclei. It binds atoms into molecules. If that force vanished, every chemical bond in your body would dissolve.
source: Standard Model of Particle Physics, CERN

text: Roughly 500,000 people are airborne globally at any typical moment.
as_written: Around the globe, roughly five hundred thousand people are in the air at any given moment, distributed across thousands of commercial flights.
source: FlightAware / Federal Aviation Administration flight statistics

text: Passenger jets at cruising altitude have roughly twenty to thirty minutes of glide time from thirty-five thousand feet.
as_written: At cruising altitude, thirty-five thousand feet up, pilots have roughly twenty to thirty minutes of glide time
source: Federal Aviation Administration (Airplane Flying Handbook FAA-H-8083-3C)

text: There are roughly one billion motor vehicles in use worldwide.
as_written: At any typical second of the day, there are roughly one billion motor vehicles on the road worldwide.
source: International Organization of Motor Vehicle Manufacturers (OICA)

text: New York City has approximately 70,000 passenger elevators.
as_written: In New York City alone, there are roughly seventy thousand passenger elevators.
source: New York City Department of Buildings

text: Undersea fiber-optic cables span over one million kilometers worldwide.
as_written: The internet, which spans over one million kilometers of undersea fiber-optic cables
source: TeleGeography Submarine Cable Map

text: Undersea fiber cables require optical repeaters every 50 to 80 kilometers.
as_written: relies on optical amplifiers placed every fifty to eighty kilometers along the seabed to boost the laser light signals.
source: SubOptic / International Telecommunication Union (ITU-T G.977)

text: More than ninety percent of global money exists exclusively in digital form.
as_written: More than ninety percent of the money in the world exists only as digital entries on bank servers, hard drives, and magnetic tapes.
source: Bank for International Settlements / Federal Reserve economic data

text: More than 40 million people worldwide with diabetes depend on insulin.
as_written: Insulin, which regulates blood sugar for more than forty million people with Type 1 and advanced Type 2 diabetes worldwide
source: World Health Organization (Global Report on Diabetes)

text: Insulin storage requires temperatures between two and eight degrees Celsius.
as_written: must be kept refrigerated between two and eight degrees Celsius to maintain its potency.
source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration / European Medicines Agency insulin guidelines

text: Approximately 3 million people worldwide suffer from end-stage renal disease and require hemodialysis.
as_written: Worldwide, there are approximately three million patients with end-stage renal disease who require mechanical hemodialysis
source: The Lancet / Global Burden of Disease Study

text: Without water, human survival is limited to three to five days under normal conditions.
as_written: survival without water is limited to three to five days.
source: National Institutes of Health / Harvard Medical School

text: There are roughly 440 commercial nuclear power reactors operating across 32 countries.
as_written: There are roughly four hundred and forty commercial nuclear power reactors operating across thirty-two countries.
source: International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Power Reactor Information System

text: Immediately after reactor scram, radioactive decay heat accounts for approximately six to seven percent of full thermal output.
as_written: Immediately after shutdown, decay heat produces roughly six to seven percent of the reactor's full thermal power.
source: Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) / American Nuclear Society Standard ANSI/ANS-5.1

text: A standard 1,000 MWe nuclear power plant produces approximately 3,000 MW of thermal power, generating roughly 200 MW of decay heat upon trip.
as_written: For a typical one-thousand-megawatt electrical plant, which generates about three thousand megawatts of thermal energy, that means nearly two hundred megawatts of heat is still being produced immediately after shutdown.
source: Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC)

text: Zirconium fuel cladding undergoes a rapid exothermic oxidation producing hydrogen at temperatures above 800 degrees Celsius.
as_written: The fuel cladding, made of a zirconium alloy, reacts with high-temperature steam once it becomes exposed to air at temperatures above eight hundred degrees Celsius.
source: International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Safety Reports Series No. 23

text: Atmospheric nitrogen makes up approximately 78 percent of the atmosphere.
as_written: While the Earth's atmosphere is roughly seventy-eight percent nitrogen
source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet

text: The Haber-Bosch process was invented in 1909.
as_written: In nineteen zero nine, German chemists Fritz Haber and Carl Bosch invented an industrial process
source: Nobel Prize in Chemistry historical archives (Fritz Haber 1918)

text: The Haber-Bosch process operates at pressures over 150 atmospheres and temperatures around 450 degrees Celsius.
as_written: under pressures exceeding one hundred and fifty atmospheres and temperatures around four hundred and fifty degrees Celsius.
source: Royal Society of Chemistry

text: The Haber-Bosch process accounts for 1 to 2 percent of global energy consumption.
as_written: Today, the Haber-Bosch process consumes roughly one to two percent of the entire world's energy supply
source: International Energy Agency (Ammonia Technology Roadmap)

text: Synthetic nitrogen fertilizer supports roughly half of the global human population.
as_written: Nearly four billion people alive right now owe their physical existence to synthetic fertilizer.
source: Our World in Data / Nature Geoscience (Erisman et al., 2008)

text: In 1900, the United States had approximately 21 million horses and draft animals for a population of 76 million.
as_written: In nineteen hundred, there were roughly twenty-one million horses and draft animals in the United States alone to support a population of seventy-six million people.
source: United States Department of Agriculture (Census of Agriculture historical data) and US Census Bureau

text: Water expands by approximately nine percent upon freezing.
as_written: expanding by approximately nine percent in volume.
source: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS Water Science School)

text: Corrosion of steel rebar creates rust that expands up to six times the volume of the original steel, creating over 5,000 psi of pressure.
as_written: Rust occupies up to six times the volume of the original steel. This massive expansion generates internal pressures exceeding five thousand pounds per square inch
source: American Concrete Institute (ACI 222R: Protection of Metals in Concrete Against Corrosion)

text: More than a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level.
as_written: In the Netherlands, more than a quarter of the land lies below sea level
source: PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency

text: The London Underground pumps out roughly 47 million liters of groundwater daily.
as_written: In London, the Tube system pumps out roughly forty-seven million liters of groundwater every single day
source: Transport for London (TfL)

text: The New York City Subway pumps out approximately 13 million gallons of groundwater daily.
as_written: In New York, the subway system pumps out approximately thirteen million gallons of water daily.
source: Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA)

text: The Carboniferous period occurred roughly 300 to 360 million years ago.
as_written: During the Carboniferous period, roughly three hundred to three hundred and sixty million years ago
source: International Commission on Stratigraphy (ICS)

text: Lignin-degrading white-rot fungi had not yet evolved during the peak Carboniferous coal deposition.
as_written: white-rot fungi capable of breaking down the complex structural polymer called lignin, had not yet evolved.
source: Science (Floudas et al., 2012, The Paleozoic Origin of Enzymatic Lignin Decomposition)

text: Edwin Drake struck commercial oil in 1859 at Titusville, Pennsylvania at a depth of 69.5 feet.
as_written: In eighteen fifty-nine, when Edwin Drake drilled the first commercial oil well in Titusville, Pennsylvania, he struck oil at a depth of just sixty-nine and a half feet below the surface.
source: Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission / Drake Well Museum
